A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DISCO work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the relocated theory and vision appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original DISCO experiments on four language benchmarks and ImageNet, including performance comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original baseline comparisons, uncertainty estimates, computational measurements and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use top-k PDS/JSD selection and model signatures with dimensionality reduction and kNN or regression prediction. Appendix I newly documents a 100-source-model subset for MMLU disagreement scoring, but does not establish that the procedure underlying the retained results changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, HellaSwag, Winogrande, ARC and ImageNet. Winogrande and ARC already appear in v1 Table 1 despite its narrower dataset-description paragraph. Additional experiments change splits and analyses within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds Lifelong Benchmark and SSEPY to the ImageNet comparison, where v1 included only random evaluation and model-signature controls alongside DISCO. These provide substantive comparisons against dedicated vision evaluation methods. The language comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds bootstrapped chronological evaluation using 346 source and 36 target models, performance-sorted splits with and without a gap, calibration measurements, and computational profiling on an H100. The stated LLM size ceiling also changes from 32B to 72B. Section 5.1 primarily documents the existing pipeline rather than establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained factor ablations, Appendices D–F test sensitivity to resampled model splits, calibration and confidence, and source–target performance gaps. Appendix B adds computational overhead and break-even analysis. These address stability, extrapolation failure and practical efficiency questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: v2 first discloses five-run averaging and reports standard deviations for fixed-split MMLU results, bootstrapped splits and computational costs. v1 lacks equivalent uncertainty reporting. The headings call these confidence intervals, but the tables report mean plus/minus standard deviation; an increase over the earlier run count is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original Table 3 rows retain their values, while substantial new results are added. ImageNet comparators obtain MAE/rank of 2.06/0.838 for Lifelong Benchmark and 3.05/0.762 for SSEPY. Under the newly tested large performance gap, Table 10 reports rank correlations of 89.2% for DISCO and 87.4% for direct evaluation. Computational, bootstrap and calibration results are also new.

T1.justification: The mutual-information identity, JSD–PDS bounds and underlying proofs are retained, largely with equivalent notation in Appendices G–H. Appendix G.0.2 adds a mathematical argument for representing nonuniform model priors through proportional model replication, a limited addition to the treatment of assumptions.

C1.justification: The central claims remain disagreement-based selection, simple signature-based prediction, information-theoretic motivation, and over 99% evaluation-cost reduction with strong prediction accuracy. The added experiments primarily support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning calibration, source-model heterogeneity, and reduced benefits under large performance gaps. It explicitly excludes open-ended generation without predefined answer choices and explains amortization of offline costs through a reported 389-evaluation break-even point. Appendix F also newly argues that large performance gaps are unrealistic.

D1.justification: Appendix I supplies previously missing hardware, output-generation tools, predictor hyperparameters, training durations and source-model subsampling details, including kNN k=1 and random-forest defaults. Appendices B and J.2 document resource requirements and vision-baseline implementations. The project and code links are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fogliato et al./SSEPY and develops the relationship to Prabhu et al.'s existing vision work. It also repositions Metabench within benchmark compression and adds dataset and implementation citations. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. Changes include wording corrections, standardized mathematical notation, an explicit stepwise evaluation protocol, separate experimental-setup subsections, and reorganized appendices. The revision mainly expands documentation rather than extensively rewriting the existing account.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–10 and three diagnostic figures, expands Table 3 with vision-baseline rows, and revises compression-plot sizing, axes and legends. The original vision figures are retained as Figures 9–10, rather than being new results displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's missing uncertainty reporting, limited vision comparisons, undocumented implementation choices and unquantified setup costs. The added robustness analyses also expose conditions where DISCO's advantage weakens. Confidence-interval labels actually denote standard deviations, and dismissing large performance gaps as unrealistic is weakly supported, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence, reproducibility and practical interpretability.
